name: Ethereal Blue
lede: Ethereal Blue is a pale, slightly grayed sky blue from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, first recorded in 1845 and closest to the core color sky blue.

sections.title: Plate 33, first seen in 1845
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary lists Ethereal Blue on plate 33, swatch E6, and dates its earliest recorded use to 1845 [1]. The same plate carries a near neighbor, Twinkle Blue, first recorded in 1927, nearly a century later [1]. Our computed match places the hue in the ISCC-NBS region called pale blue, Munsell notation 9.6B 7.0/3.3 [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[russian-blue]], [[light-alice-blue]], [[pewter-blue]] and [[watteau]], at 2.5, 3, 3 and 3.8 ΔE [2]. It reads paler and grayer than a plain [[blue]], closer to a hazy, overcast version of [[sky-blue]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Ethereal Blue covers at least five percent of the canvas in 248 of them, about 1 percent overall, as photographed [3]. Use rises sharply in the 1870s, over twice the archive average, and is strongest among Impressionists: Childe Hassam and Pierre Puvis de Chavannes each carry it well above twenty times the average rate [3]. Nearly four in five of its appearances are highlights rather than shadow, and it keeps company most with the company word Sky blue [3]. These counts are read from photographs of varnished paintings [3].
